_meta.indication: Temporary improvement in the appearance of moderate to severe glabellar lines associated with corrugator and/or procerus muscle activity in adult patients

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of identical design, randomized 3 to 1 to a single treatment with LETYBO or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy adults (age 19 to 75) with glabellar lines of at least moderate severity at maximum frown
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving a score of 0 or 1 and an improvement of at least 2 points from baseline at maximum frown at Week 4, assessed by both investigator and subject on the Glabellar Line Scale (GLS)
pivotal_trials.n: BLESS I: LETYBO N=528, Placebo N=175 (pooled across BLESS I, II, III: 1,276 enrolled)
pivotal_trials.result: BLESS I treatment success (multi-component): 47% LETYBO vs 0% placebo; treatment difference 47% (95% CI 43%, 51%)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of identical design
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy adults (age 19 to 75) with glabellar lines of at least moderate severity at maximum frown
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion achieving GLS 0 or 1 and improvement of at least 2 points from baseline at maximum frown at Week 4, by both investigator and subject
pivotal_trials.n: BLESS II: LETYBO N=160, Placebo N=53
pivotal_trials.result: BLESS II treatment success: 49% LETYBO vs 2% placebo; treatment difference 45% (95% CI 36%, 54%)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of identical design
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy adults (age 19 to 75) with glabellar lines of at least moderate severity at maximum frown
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion achieving GLS 0 or 1 and improvement of at least 2 points from baseline at maximum frown at Week 4, by both investigator and subject
pivotal_trials.n: BLESS III: LETYBO N=266, Placebo N=89
pivotal_trials.result: BLESS III treatment success: 65% LETYBO vs 0% placebo; treatment difference 65% (95% CI 59%, 71%)

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction was headache (2% LETYBO vs 1% placebo; 17/911 vs 2/310); brow ptosis, eyelid ptosis and blepharospasm each <1%. Serious risks include distant spread of toxin effect with swallowing/breathing difficulties that can be life threatening.
target_moa: LetibotulinumtoxinA blocks the release of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine at peripheral cholinergic nerve terminals, inducing muscle paralysis following intramuscular injection; it is an acetylcholine release inhibitor and neuromuscular blocking agent
modality: Botulinum toxin type A neurotoxin complex (protein biologic; noncovalent multimeric complex of 6 proteins, ~900 kDa)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: DISTANT SPREAD OF TOXIN EFFECT — effects may spread from the injection area to produce botulinum toxin effects; swallowing and breathing difficulties can be life threatening with reports of death

rems.type: REMS will not be required for this application

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; the review team determined the product presented no novel or complex issues requiring input

summary.text: Standard BLA 761225 under section 351(a); reviewed by the Division of Dermatology and Dentistry. The application was not referred to an advisory committee. It was approved after prior Complete Response cycles related to manufacturing facility deficiencies, with a postmarketing commitment (PMC 761225-01) to investigate a non-animal-based potency assay (final report 12/2028).

citations.quote: The Applicant has submitted an original BLA under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act for its product, letibotulinumtoxinA, for the temporary improvement in the appearance of moderate to severe glabellar lines associated with corrugator and/or procerus muscle activity in adults.

Your application for Letybo was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a biologic of this class.

the product quality team recommended a PMC 761225-01: To investigate the development and implementation of a non-animal-based potency assay for drug substance and drug product release and stability testing with the final report submission in 12/2028.
